friction: The caller contract cannot express the edit it certifies: with 74% of columns gone, request.json carries only flags, Equal, the 4,792-pair projection (repeated three times) and inverse indices, so the deletion is bound solely by claim 0's 18,380 inverse identities and claim 1's 576 source-row checks; no API call can state or check 'target = source minus these columns and rows for these reasons'.

Homogeneous obligations are hand-emitted one at a time: 6,306 Cases steps, 2,529,170 Lin terms and a 60,099-node shared subset tree produce a 17.0 MB RPA / 11.5 MB RPX to displace 0.17 MB of caller claims; the case script had to invent its own premise memo (weighted_subset/all_except) and id counter to keep this tractable.

Structure discovery is not in the API: the 30 one-hot groups, 426-row capacity family with 168 dominated members, and the 60-edge DAG transitive reduction were recovered by hand-written eval scanners and then passed to the proof as untrusted audit.json hints, which the preparer has to re-assert against the canonical model (lines 38,43,68).

Check atoms are positional and each premise index must be re-derived by the generator: the case code asserts child.refexpr(ref)==wanted and asserts witness coefficients equal the audit values (lines 20-21,43,68,81-82); blocks 1-2 rebuild their own builders and re-derive all their facts because locals are block-scoped, so nothing about the 6,306 zero facts can be shared across blocks.

Negative testing is dict surgery on a full-size certificate: each of the five mutations rewrites the whole 17 MB RPA, re-assembles, re-verifies and deletes the artifacts (lines 124-134), and locating the target step needs the audit hint file re-read inside the mutation branch (line 129). Attribution is only the message text ('expected Le; obligation 55231', 'expected Int; obligation 8').
